findings.title: Affection against borrowed patronage
findings.claim: The focus form وُدًّا carries affection as what al-Rahman makes for those who trust and do righteous deeds. The pericope places that gift beside a denier’s projected wealth and offspring, acquired gods meant to furnish honor, and the fracture following a false filial claim; the next verse’s easy message and opposed hearers add a bounded public-speech contact, while the same form allows an echo of the Wadd idol-name.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb yajʿalu makes wudd a relation assigned for the believing and acting group. Earlier claims and failed patrons supply independent counter-scenes; the good-deed and trust terms connect the gift to conduct. In 19:97 the message is made easy on the tongue to bring good news and warning to different hearers, letting the focus’s affection sit within a publicly disclosed response. The wishing branch lets affection remain a desired outcome, while the idol-name branch makes the focus form resonate with the pericope’s false-god scene.
findings.reader_payoff: Affection appears as a made social good set against promised possessions and borrowed honor, and as a relation whose hearers are made public through the adjacent message; the additional lexical echoes do not replace its ordinary sense.
findings.containment: The ordinary affection reading remains primary and recoverable. The context says generic false gods and never names Wadd, so the proper-name connection is a qualified echo, not a claim that 19:81 names that idol. The wishing branch describes a possible outcome resonance, not a substitution of wishing for affection.
